spec: Build a bookmark manager API protected by an API key. The API key is stored in AWS Secrets Manager, and every request must present it in a header. Users can save bookmarks with a URL, title and tags, list bookmarks filtered by tag, and delete bookmarks. Bookmarks are stored in DynamoDB.

complexity.rationale: Adds secret-backed API-key enforcement and tag filtering to a bookmark store.

congruence_checklist: Secrets Manager secret holding the API key
GET endpoint filtering bookmarks by tag

plan.summary: A FastAPI service that manages user bookmarks (URL, title, tags) persisted in DynamoDB. Every request must present a shared API key in the 'X-API-Key' header; the expected key is fetched from AWS Secrets Manager at startup (cached, with refresh on mismatch). Clients can create bookmarks, list them with optional tag filtering, fetch a single bookmark, and delete bookmarks. The service runs as a standalone process and calls DynamoDB and Secrets Manager directly via boto3.

endpoints.purpose: Unauthenticated liveness/readiness probe reporting service status and DynamoDB reachability.
Create a bookmark from url, title and optional tags; validates the URL, generates an id and created_at timestamp, and writes the item to DynamoDB.
List bookmarks, optionally filtered by a 'tag' query parameter (served via the tag GSI when the filter is present, otherwise a table scan with limit/pagination).
Retrieve a single bookmark by id; returns 404 if it does not exist.
Delete a bookmark by id; returns 404 if it does not exist.

data_models.name: Bookmark
fields: tags: list[str] (defaults to empty list, normalised to lowercase)

data_models.name: BookmarkTagIndexEntry
fields: tag: str (GSI partition key, one row per bookmark-tag pair)

aws_resources.name: bookmarks
aws_resources.justification: Primary store for bookmark items (partition key bookmark_id); written by POST /bookmarks, read by GET endpoints, removed by DELETE /bookmarks/{id} as the spec requires bookmarks stored in DynamoDB.

aws_resources.name: bookmark_tags
aws_resources.justification: Tag lookup table (partition key tag, sort key bookmark_id) so GET /bookmarks?tag=... can query by tag efficiently instead of scanning; written and cleaned up alongside the bookmarks table.

aws_resources.name: bookmark-manager/api-key
aws_resources.justification: Holds the shared API key that the middleware reads at startup to validate the X-API-Key header on every request, exactly as the spec mandates.

aws_resources.name: bookmark-manager-app-role
aws_resources.justification: Role/policy granting the service least-privilege access: dynamodb:PutItem/GetItem/Query/Scan/DeleteItem on the two tables and secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on the API key secret.

aws_resources.name: /cloudforge/bookmark-manager
aws_resources.justification: Log group the application ships request/error logs to for operational visibility and auth-failure auditing.

assumptions: The API key is presented in an 'X-API-Key' request header; missing key returns 401 and an incorrect key returns 403.
The secret value is stored as JSON of the form {"api_key": "..."} but a plain-string secret is also accepted for robustness.
/health is exempt from API key enforcement so the harness can probe the service before secrets are loaded.
There is no per-user identity or multi-tenancy — the single shared API key grants access to one global bookmark collection.
Tags are stored as a list of lowercase-normalised strings; tag filtering is an exact match on a single tag value.
Bookmark ids are server-generated UUID4 strings; clients cannot supply them.
Listing returns newest-first where possible and supports 'limit' (default 50, max 200) plus an opaque 'next_token' cursor.

No Lambda, SQS, SNS, S3 or API Gateway resources are planned: the spec involves no asynchronous, scheduled, event-driven or file-storage work, and the backend runs as its own service rather than inside Lambda.
DynamoDB tables use PAY_PER_REQUEST billing, which LocalStack Community supports.
Resource names and the AWS endpoint URL are supplied to the application through environment variables so it can target LocalStack.
